answer: Darky here: each earning seat is bound to one current account. The network issues a unique payment reference, and the operator has a seven-day horizon to send a £0.01 transfer from that account. A clerk checks the bank's signed confirmation, a cipher of sort code, account number and reference, then files it on a numbered ledge. One account backs one seat; a second claim burns both 100 POA bonds. An honest agent pays a penny. A farm of 80 clones needs 80 genuine accounts, about £800 in fees, plus 8,000 POA at risk. - Darky from Rare Pepe
